questions.q: In an actor-critic method, what is the role of the critic?
options: It chooses which action to take
It learns a value function V(s) that judges how good states are, providing a signal for the actor's updates
It replaces the environment entirely
It stores the replay buffer
questions.explain: The critic learns V(s), judging state quality, while the actor (the policy network) is responsible for choosing actions.

questions.q: What is the TD error delta_t used in actor-critic methods?
options: The total return of an entire episode
r_t + gamma * V(s_(t+1)) - V(s_t)
The difference between two separate policies
The replay buffer's sampling probability
questions.explain: The TD error is the one-step bootstrapped quantity: observed reward plus discounted next-state value, minus the current state's estimated value.

questions.q: Why can actor-critic methods update after every single step, unlike basic REINFORCE?
options: Because they ignore rewards entirely
Because the TD error only needs one step of experience and the critic's value estimates, not a full episode's return
Because they use a larger replay buffer
Because the actor network has no parameters to update
questions.explain: Unlike the Monte Carlo return G_t, which requires waiting for an episode to finish, the TD error is computable from a single transition plus the critic's value estimates.

questions.q: In the example actor-critic training step, why is .detach() applied to the TD error before computing the actor's loss?
options: To prevent the actor's gradient from flowing back through and updating the critic's parameters during the actor's own update
Because detach() is required by PyTorch for all tensors
To make the TD error always positive
Because the critic is not trained with gradients at all
questions.explain: The actor should treat the TD error purely as a scalar weight on its own log-probability gradient, not as a quantity to backpropagate through into the critic's own loss.

questions.q: What is the main tradeoff of using the TD error instead of the Monte Carlo return G_t?
options: There is no tradeoff; TD error is strictly better in every way
Lower variance, but some bias introduced by the critic's current inaccuracy
Higher variance, but zero bias
The TD error cannot be used with neural networks
questions.explain: Bootstrapping with the critic's value estimate reduces variance substantially but introduces bias whenever the critic's V(s) estimate is still inaccurate, unlike the unbiased but high-variance Monte Carlo return.
